driftNotes: make known > recognize > range of knowledge or sight ('beyond one's ken') > crisp monosyllable for knowledge products; archaic-Scots warmth keeps it human, not academic.
to see > to know > the living senses ('five wits') > facile cleverness; shared root with video/vision — a nimble-mind brand that predates the joke.

layers.ancientGreek: noētikos (νοητικός, of the intellect), from nous (νους, mind)
layers.classicalLatin: noeticus (post-classical philosophical Latin rendering of Greek noētikos)

driftNotes: Greek nous (mind, intellect) > noēsis, an act of thinking > the philosopher's adjective for pure intellection; sleek Greek abstraction with built-in intelligence signal.
counting > reckoning an account > measured judgment > faculty of thinking; same root as arithmetic — a considered-judgment brand with ledger-quality calm.
goddess of the arts > absorbed contemplation > the wellspring a creator waits on; names the spark itself rather than the output — a patron-saint register for tools.
to weigh on a scale > to weigh in the mind; deliberate, unhurried gravity — thinking as careful measurement, anti-skim by construction.
outstretched arms > embrace > sounding water one arm-span at a time > to understand deeply; comprehension measured by what the arms can circle.
furrow to follow > teaching handed down the track > a people's body of knowledge; heirloom expertise — 'folklore' warmth without 'knowledge' bureaucracy.
making visible > apparition > imagination > taste and light whim; a playful, design-forward word that hides a gleaming apparition inside.
spadework in soil > burrowing into books and questions; research with dirt under its nails — tool-grade word for investigative products.
breath > the wind inside a living thing > soul; also Jung's inner self — vital-breath premium with optional depth-psychology resonance.
breath of life > the whole inner life; in Greek the word also named the butterfly, so soul and metamorphosis share one glyph — change-ready wellness register.
a divine nod of assent > indwelling power in a place or thing (whence 'numinous'); quiet sacred authority without any doctrine attached.
custom and habit > the character a community lives by > Aristotle's credibility-of-speaker; culture made audible — trust as an audible trait.
the organ > seat of feeling and courage ('take heart') > sincerity itself ('heartfelt'); the warmest monosyllable in the language, cognate with Latin cor.
strength > price and worth > bravery proven under pressure; courage with an honor-and-worth ledger inside, cognate with 'value' and 'valid'.
breath > animating vapor > courage and distilled essence ('spirits' of wine); liveliness and distillation in one word — essence with a heartbeat.
Germanic life-spirit > moral and emotional core > depth of feeling (soul food, soul music); authenticity shorthand — warm, human, unpretentious.
cooling breeze > subtle vapor and fragrance > the atmosphere a person or place radiates; vibe rendered premium — presence you can feel but not see.
rain-bearing cloud > the golden disc behind saints > a charisma-cloud around a person or brand; atmosphere with a luminous edge, not weather tech.
glowing white > purity > frank openness; bright-honest sheen from the same gleam as 'candle' — a transparent brand voice.
public esteem and high office > reputation kept as moral stature > integrity one does not trade; plainspoken dignity, weight of the Roman cursus.
wages earned > service that earns favor > deserved standing; fairness you can measure — the anti-pedigree, pay-for-what-you-earn virtue.
physical stiffness > exactness of logic > severity admired; the straightening root also yields rex and regulate — precision with a spine.
favor freely given > pleasing elegance of form > poise under pressure ('saving grace'); unearned goodwill — generous warmth with a thankful root (grateful, gratitude).

layers.classicalLatin: temperare (to mix in due proportion), temperantia (moderation)

driftNotes: mixing in due measure (steel, seasons) > self-restraint > composure ('lose one's temper' inverts it); the smith's and the sage's shared word for disciplined balance.
proven good > morally tested > scrupulous honesty; same root as 'proof' and 'probation' — integrity with receipts.
truth > sincerity of statement ('in verity') > enduring principles; a fact-forward brand carrying Chaucer's medieval patina, kin to German 'wahr'.
love (amare) > friendship > treaty of goodwill between peoples; diplomatic warmth — goodwill as infrastructure, kin to 'amiable' and 'amigo'.
level ground > impartial law (the chancery sense) > modern fairness plus ownership stake; one word that levels the field and owns the upside.

layers.ancientGreek: logikē (λογική, art of reason), logos (λόγος, word, reason)

driftNotes: gathering words > reasoned account > formal science of inference; rides logos, the deepest carrier in Greek philosophy — systems-thinker sobriety.

layers.ancientGreek: prisma (πρίσμα, thing sawn), priein (πρίειν, to saw)

driftNotes: sawn-off block > geometry solid > Newton's light-splitter; takes one input and reveals its hidden spectrum — analytic brilliance with a literal cut edge.
becoming acquainted with a thing > any formed idea > a passing whim; same know-root as 'note' and 'cognition' — idea-stage clarity, concept before cathedral.
the act of teaching > a body of principles > a codified stance; scholarly authority — kin to 'doctor' and 'docile', a stance you can cite.
watching a festival rite as an official spectator (theōros) > contemplation > systematic account of things; festival-watching became science — thought as spectacle.

layers.ancientGreek: axiōma (ἀξίωμα, thing thought worthy), axios (ἄξιος, worthy)

driftNotes: what weighs enough to be worthy > a self-evident starting point; bedrock certainty — first-principles packaging, kin to 'axle' and 'axis'.
the 'greatest proposition' of a philosopher > pithy rule of conduct; compressed ancestral wisdom in two syllables — aphorism with superlative bones (maximum, Magnus).
'it holds' — the verb's third person became the noun for a belief held firm; famous from the Sator palindrome square, doctrine you hold rather than a creed you recite.

layers.ancientGreek: thesis (θέσις, a setting down), tithenai (τίθημι, to place)

driftNotes: a placing of the foot, of a stone > a position staked > a proposition to defend; arguments laid like masonry — strong for decision-tools and research products.

layers.classicalLatin: caudex (tree trunk) → codex (wooden tablets, bound book, law ledger)
layers.middleEnglish: codex (bound volume of sacred or legal texts)

driftNotes: hewn trunk > wax tablets bound together > the bound book that killed the scroll; a format revolution made word — canonical, structured, durable knowledge.

layers.classicalLatin: fervor (boiling heat, ardor), fervere (to boil, glow)

driftNotes: literal boil > heat of zeal; keeps the pot-on-stove image (kin to 'brew' and 'effervesce') — passion you can measure in bubbles.
flame > consuming fire > consuming devotion; from the same burn-root as 'ash' and 'ardent' — refined brand-heat, more elegant than raw 'fire'.
market wages (kin to 'merchant') > the heavenly reward for kindness > forbearance shown when power is asymmetric; commerce transformed into grace.
eager wanting > the ache of longing (its old moral edge quietly dropped); hunger that stays noble — desire without grasping, strong for mission brands.

layers.ancientGreek: empatheia (ἐμπάθεια, strong feeling); em- (in) + pathos (πάθος, feeling)
layers.classicalLatin: pathos (πάθος, suffering/experience — root borrowed into philosophical Latin for Greek affect-terminology)

driftNotes: coined in 1904 to render German Einfühlung ('feeling into' a painting) > psychology's emotion-sharing > the listening superpower; a modern coin on ancient parts.
emulation and rivalry (it could curdle into 'jealousy') > fervent dedication; concentrated drive with a spicy ancient edge — kin to 'zealot', so the fire is built in.
enduring what befalls you > the Passion narrative > any overwhelming emotion > what you cannot not do; endurance turned all-consuming — gravity, not hype.
raving, wandering speech > wild delight and revelry > the soft daydream state; the brainstorm-before-focus mood — creative products use the calm sense.
what befalls one > the emotion an orator stirs; Aristotle's heart-string member of the ethos–pathos–logos trio — feeling as a design material.
terror before the numinous > reverential wonder with a tremor kept inside; three letters from fear to wonderment — 'awesome' is its diluted descendant.

layers.middleEnglish: aimen (to estimate; to direct at a target)

driftNotes: appraising value > judging distance > pointing at a target; kin to 'esteem' and 'estimate' — calculation made directional, goal-setting with a valuer's eye.
seeking and asking > the hunt for game > the chivalric search for the Grail; a question wearing armor — inquiry framed as adventure, kin to 'query' and 'inquest'.
following forward > the chase (and the prosecution bench — same root as 'prosecute') > a dedicated endeavor; motion toward, never mere wanting.
straining toward > fixed attention > purpose with resolve implied; a drawn bow, not a decision memo — directional brother of 'tend', 'tension', and 'attend'.

layers.middleEnglish: striven (to quarrel; to struggle, try hard)

driftNotes: quarrel and contention > the fight redirected inward as effort; 'strife' tamed into aspiration — exertion as channeled combat, effort with a warrior past.

layers.classicalLatin: advenire (to arrive), adventura (things about to come)

driftNotes: what-is-about-to-come > happening by chance > risking oneself on the coming thing; the future treated as terrain — bold without being finance-locked.
the sending of envoys and friars > a personal calling or undertaking; you don't merely have a mission, you're sent on one — purpose with a dispatch built in.
the trampled sill that kept threshed grain in > point of entry > the limit where a new state begins (pain threshold); doorway physics becoming psychology — crossings and new regimes.

layers.ancientGreek: idea (ἰδέα, form, semblance), idein (ἰδεῖν, to see)

driftNotes: something seen > Plato's form beyond sight > the perfect exemplar one strives toward; aspiration with a philosopher's passport — the visible made into a standard.
the bounding line where earth finishes > the circle that meets the sky > the limit of sight and knowledge ('expand your horizons'); a boundary that recedes as you advance — hope with geometry.
